items.exemplar:
A. The Truman Doctrine (1947) pledged American aid to any nation resisting communism, first applied to Greece and Turkey.

B. The Marshall Plan poured $13 billion into Western Europe's recovery to keep war-ravaged nations from turning Communist, and NATO (1949) bound America to Europe's defense.

C. At home, Truman's loyalty program investigated federal employees, HUAC probed Hollywood and government, and McCarthyism purged suspected communists from public life.
parts: A. Briefly explain ONE American effort to contain communism overseas, 1945–1960.
B. Briefly explain a SECOND such overseas effort.
C. Briefly explain ONE effort to combat communism within the United States in the same period.

Questioner: Can you describe the military information you obtained through the Silvermaster group? Bentley: I passed along classified material on aircraft production and other defense matters, gathered from government employees sympathetic to the Soviet cause.
—After Elizabeth Bentley's testimony before the House Committee on Un-American Activities, 1948 (paraphrased)
